title: Community pharmacy collaborative prescribing: Schedule II through V bar and Schedule VI authorization
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 16.03(5)(e)3., no authorized pharmacist in a community pharmacy may prescribe or be authorized to prescribe Schedule II through V controlled substances, as defined in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 3, subsections (2) through (5). Under 247 CMR 16.03(5)(e)4., an authorized pharmacist in a community pharmacy may be authorized by a supervising physician to issue prescriptions for Schedule VI controlled substances, as defined in M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 3, subsection (6), for the diagnoses specified in the supervising physician's patient referral. 243 CMR 2.12(4)(e)7. and 8. state the same bar and authorization.
exam_relevance: Tests that the regulations bar both the prescribing and the authorizing of Schedule II through V substances in a community pharmacy, and tie Schedule VI prescriptions to the diagnoses in the referral.

authority.name: Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations
Board of Registration in Medicine regulations

common_confusions: The bar is stated twice over: the pharmacist may not prescribe Schedule II through V substances, and may not be authorized to prescribe them, so an agreement term purporting to authorize it confers nothing.
Schedule V is inside the bar; the range is Schedule II through V.
Schedule VI authority is something the supervising physician may confer, and it is confined to the diagnoses specified in the supervising physician's patient referral.
verification_notes: Read in the current mass.gov PDF of 247 CMR 16.00 (regulation page dated 12/15/2017) and in the current mass.gov PDF of 243 CMR 2.00 on 2026-09-17.
